text: Code reviews are an essential practice in software development. When a developer finishes writing a piece of code, another team member carefully examines it before it is merged into the main project. The main benefit is catching bugs early. Small mistakes, like logic errors or missing edge cases, are far cheaper to fix at this stage than after the code reaches users. Beyond finding errors, code reviews are a powerful tool for knowledge sharing. Team members learn new techniques and understand different parts of the codebase they might never have explored. This process also naturally improves overall team quality, as everyone writes more carefully knowing their work will be reviewed, and consistent standards are reinforced across the whole team.
